LESSON: MULTI-PURPOSE RIVER PROJECTS IN AFRICA • RIVER TANA PROJECTS IN KENYA • ASWAN HIGH DAM IN EGYPT

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments
Topic 4.3: Multi-purpose River Projects in Africa • River Tana Projects in Kenya • Aswan High Dam in Egypt
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Multi-purpose River Projects in Africa • River Tana Projects in Kenya • Aswan High Dam in Egypt, part of Natural and Historic Built Environments in Grade 9 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How useful are multi-purpose river projects in society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Multi-purpose River Projects in Africa • River Tana Projects in Kenya • Aswan High Dam in Egypt together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: learners use digital resources to identify selected multi-purpose river projects (River Tana Projects in Kenya,

Aswan High Dam in Egypt).

• Communication and Collaboration: learners discuss the conditions that led to the establishment of multi-purpose river projects

along river Tana.

Values:
• Responsibility: learners suggest solutions to challenges facing multipurpose river projects.

• Social Justice: learners foster inclusivity and non-discrimination as they discuss the conditions that led to the establishment of

multi-purpose river projects along river Tana.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Creative thinking skills: learners engage with a resource person to share on the solutions to challenges facing multipurpose

river projects.

• Financial Literacy: learners brainstorm in groups on the economic importance of multi-purpose river projects in Africa and

write short notes.

Link to other Learning Areas:

• Learners apply Agriculture knowledge to brainstorm on the economic importance of multi-purpose river projects in Africa

and write short notes.

• Learners use Kenyan Sign Language, English, and Kiswahili knowledge to discuss the conditions that led to the establishment

of multi-purpose river projects along river Tana.
